thesis: The post-earnings gap has already been paid for: price (29.10) sits above the mean analyst target (24.5), and the 11-06 spike to 31.00 closed at 28.49, a rejection at the 52-week high. The first resistance gives only about 1.4 R/R, so the 2.26 headline ratio depends on a breakout. Cash conversion is weak (FCF 9.2M on 13.3% margin) and debt is sizeable, so the cheap multiples may reflect low earnings quality. With the regime risk-off at 0.85 confidence, a 21.7% short-interest name that has run +34% in 63 days is exposed to sharp reversals, and the news support is thin (one substantive article). Post-earnings drift and a catalyst-free 20-day window leave nothing to push it through 31.
